Keys: spotlight follows the slide's presenter; 1 to 6 or P switches speaker by hand, 0 back to automatic (or click a name at the top) · M music · D duck under your voice · F fade out · [ and ] volume · V this panel · T trailer · N notes · S notes window.
Playing to the Bluetooth speaker and the classroom speakers at once. One audio output goes out of this page, so route it at the laptop. Mac: open Audio MIDI Setup, press + and choose Create Multi-Output Device, tick the HDMI output and the Bluetooth speaker, tick Drift Correction on the Bluetooth one, then pick that Multi-Output Device in System Settings, Sound, Output. Windows: Windows cannot send one app to two outputs by itself. Use a free tool such as VoiceMeeter, or set the Bluetooth speaker as Output, then in Sound settings, Recording, Stereo Mix, Properties, Listen, tick Listen to this device and choose HDMI. Delay warning: Bluetooth runs about a quarter of a second behind HDMI. On a steady drone that is fine; on hits and the heartbeat it sounds like an echo. If it does, press the Hits button to turn them off, or use the fallback. Fallback: send sound to HDMI only (classroom speakers) and keep the music low. Or play the music from a phone on the Bluetooth speaker and leave this page muted (M).
